author: kurokku
quote:
I waited 13 years for this, paid full price, and honestly? I feel straight-up scammed. Don't get me wrong, Vice City looks insane, and all those fake 10/10 review scores from big outlets made me think we were getting the game of the century. But once you actually boot it up, it’s not Grand Theft Auto .it’s a laggy, overpriced 9-to-5 dating and chore simulator.
First off, playing a massive AAA game in late 2026 locked at 30 FPS with zero performance mode is a complete joke. On my OLED TV, fast driving and camera pans turn into a blurry, juddery mess. Even worse, my base PS5 can't even hold 30 FPS—blow up a few cars or start a big police chase and the frame rate tanks to 25 FPS and stutters like crazy. On top of that, the driving feels weirdly clunky and unnecessarily frustrating.
The story and characters are the biggest letdown, though. You can immediately tell the original writers behind GTA 5 and Red Dead left Rockstar years ago. The plot has terrible pacing and completely falls apart by the end. Jason has zero soul—he’s literally like Jon Snow in the final season of Game of Thrones, just nodding along saying "yeah" and "yes, my queen" while Lucia constantly nags him. None of the side characters are memorable either.
Worst of all, the first 10 to 20 hours are pure misery. GTA 5 started with an epic bank heist; GTA 6 forces you to spend three or four evenings picking up Lucia's laundry, buying groceries (with an unskippable cutscene just to carry bags inside), buying her flowers, flipping burgers, getting a gym membership to work out, and fixing a house with quick-time events. I didn't wait 13 years to play The Sims—I can do chores in real life for free. Throw in running back to your car trunk for heavy weapons, an overly punishing police heat system, no online mode at launch, and a "physical" box with just a download code inside, and it's an absolute disaster.
Pretty graphics can't save a broken, soulless chore simulator. 2/10
